prompts.southernHighRoad:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Bell Before Dusk top-down exploration map, SOUTHERN HIGH ROAD.
Reference image 1 is the exact existing game rendering reference: preserve its sharp black linework, textured dirt, readable rocks and plants, pixel-like painted detail, elevated orthographic camera and constant object scale. Change biome and topology.
Create one complete larger portrait game map, requested 1280x1920 pixels, slightly larger traversable world than the existing 1024x1536 forest field at equal character scale. Early Edo rural Japan: open grassland, harvested fields, rectangular rice paddies along outer edges, low earthen banks, scattered pines and willows, roadside travel shelter and weathered milestones. Dry ochre road, muted straw and olive-green grasses, slate stone, restrained amber lanterns. No dense enclosing forest.
GAME GEOMETRY: broad north/south central travel road merging into a very wide open grassy/dirt common, occupying 75% of the image. Exactly one broad straight east/west crossroads through the middle. Roads have rectangular orthogonal junctions, never diagonal curves. The large center is fully traversable, with only two small sparse rock clusters. Plants in the playable center remain short. Road exits are centered top and bottom, and one broad east exit halfway down to a platformer. Visible frame along outer edges is made of low stone walls, peripheral paddy water, hedges and rocks. Water only at outer edges, no interior channels or fake tiny crossings. Left edge small rest shelter opens directly onto broad ground, with no hidden or inaccessible-looking alley. No sky or horizon; the entire image is an orthographic playable map. Buildings stay against edges. Gates are simple roadside barriers, not elaborate temple portals.
No characters, enemies, pickups, bells, HUD, labels, text, watermark, decorative inaccessible paths, isometric vanishing point, or white artifacts. This is a production environment illustration with clear traversable floor.
prompts.harvestLeveeA:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Bell Before Dusk platformer 4, Harvest Levee, terrain panel A of two.
Style reference 1 controls exact black-outline weight, detailed painted pixel-art texture, orthographic SIDE VIEW, sharp landable edges and transparent canvas. Blueprint reference 2 controls platform geometry. Translate cedar woodland materials into rural earth, fieldstone and timber, retaining exact geometry of THREE HORIZONTAL LANDING BANDS. It is not a forest.
Draw at 2172x724. Lowest band is continuous solid embankment, top at y570, earth body down to bottom. Middle one-way landing decks: x0–900 and x1040–2020, top y410, 54 pixels thick. Upper decks: x210–1130 and x1320–2172, top y250, 54 pixels thick. Preserve gaps and empty vertical passages; these are thin parallel platforms suspended with open air below. A player can jump up through decks and land on their top edges. No collision geometry connecting levels. No ramps or stairs.
Material: warm ochre packed-earth caps, dark fieldstone fronts, timber sluice supports, short straw grass on edges. Sparse rice bundles and thin reeds behind edges only, no decoration intruding into player standing room. Preserve the game's dark ink outlines and olive/moss shading. Do not turn decks into islands with enormous hanging rocks. Last 200px at right is clean repeatable landing surface at each blueprint band for stitching to next panel.
Genuine transparency outside terrain. No backgrounds, sky, horizon, trees, characters, enemies, UI, text, bells, labels, white fringe, water across walking floor, diagonal ramps, wedges, or fourth lane.
prompts.harvestLeveeACleanup:

Edit this game terrain asset. Remove ALL bright red pixels, red fringes, red matte specks and red patches around every terrain silhouette. Replace red edge contamination with clean black/dark-brown outline or actual transparency. Preserve the original three horizontal platform bands, their positions, the bottom floor, golden harvest palette, wood, stone and grass detail exactly. Background outside terrain must be genuinely transparent, including holes between decks. Do not add anything. No red, pink, magenta or white edge halo anywhere. Requested canvas 2172x724; preserve proportions.
prompts.harvestLeveeB:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Harvest Levee platformer PANEL B, continuation of reference panel A, requested 2172x724 with actual alpha transparency.
Use reference 1 as exact style, deck construction, palette and scale reference, and reference 2 as exact geometric layout reference. Make the second half of a 4344x724 side-scrolling course. Three repeated horizontal landing bands; continuous bottom embankment; staggered thin middle and upper decks with open air beneath them. Match panel A's walkable surface heights at the seam: upper band y250, middle band y410, bottom y570. Blueprint sets the breaks. Rural early Edo farmland, straw-gold grass, ochre earth tops, dark brown timber deck fronts, fieldstone foundation, very sparse rice bundles. Same crisp dark outlines and painted pixel-art detail as panel A. Flat long landing surfaces and small short jump gaps. One modest wooden road exit post at far right of lowest band. Keep player standing space open. No forest, stairs, ramps, wedges, hills, extra lanes, huge plants, characters, UI, labels or words. Transparent between bands and outside terrain; keep edge RGB dark brown/black, no colored matte or white halos.
prompts.banditStorehouseA:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: Bell Before Dusk platformer 5, Bandit Storehouse, PANEL A of two; transparent game terrain requested 2172x724.
Use reference1 to lock the game's detailed painted pixel-art style, black linework and flat side-view. Use reference2 for three horizontal landing-band layout with long platforms and staggered gaps. Build an early Edo fortified rice-storehouse course using dark timber galleries, wooden fighting decks, blackened fieldstone and tiny muted rust-red cloth accents. This stage is architecture, not forest or floating moss islands.
There must be a continuous lowest courtyard floor at y570, two long middle gallery platforms top y410, and two long upper timber platforms top y250. Gallery decks are flat, 50–60px thick and open beneath. The middle band has a gap near x950, the top has a gap near x1200, so changing floors changes routes. Do not stack solid walls that prevent jumping between bands. Background structural beams may be narrow and sparse; keep the majority of space between floors transparent. At x0 lower floor one small entrance frame behind landing area; right edge upper deck continues for joining panelB. Only small crates behind decks, never obstruct walkable edges. Flat short roof eaves may trim deck fronts but NO sloped roof as a walkable platform. Keep same character scale as the reference, comfortable headroom on each floor. Strong dark outer stroke, dark neutral edge RGB under alpha.
No ramps, wedges, stairs, trees, bells, spikes, hazards baked into terrain, characters, UI, labels, writing or white halo. Transparent background outside terrain. All three bands are landable gameplay geometry.

Build three parallel landing bands: continuous lowest stone courtyard floor top y570, middle thin wood gallery top y410, upper thin wood gallery top y250. Strong dark ink linework, original detailed painted pixel-art materials matching the existing game.
